real_qa.q: What was Denver apartment construction delivery in 2024 compared to historical averages?
real_qa.r: Denver delivered 23,000 apartment units in 2024, compared to a previous natural governor of about 13,500 units annually and a historical high of 13,000 units delivered in 2018. This represented an unprecedented spike driven by pent-up permitting and development from during COVID.

real_qa.q: What is the current stabilized apartment vacancy rate in Denver in Q2 2026?
real_qa.r: Stabilized vacancy in Denver was 6.32% in Q2 2026, down 115 basis points quarter over quarter and down 7 basis points year over year, representing a huge reduction from 7.27% the prior quarter.

real_qa.q: Why did Denver apartment absorption spike in 2021 despite out-migration and flat population growth?
real_qa.r: During 2021, despite essentially zero population growth due to out-migration matching natural change, Denver set historic apartment absorption numbers because as the economy deteriorated, renting became a more affordable option than buying, pushing people from the for-sale product into the rental market.

real_qa.q: What is the median home price in Denver and how does it compare to the national average?
real_qa.r: The median home price in Denver is $650,000, which is 56% above the national average. This compares to 2005 when Denver's median home price was only 13% above the national average, showing significant appreciation relative to national housing markets.

real_qa.q: What percentage of Denver's apartment stock was built during the 2010s?
